venue: Journal of the Optical Society of America B 34(3):613-624
material_system: generic dielectric channel waveguides (numerical examples: rectangular straight channels)
core_dimensions: not stated in accessible abstract (example: rectangular straight channels)
grid_or_solver_settings: not accessible (full text closed). Author presentation states: channel eigenmodes computed numerically, amplitude functions discretised by 1-D linear finite elements, Galerkin weak form of Maxwell equations assembled into K_uu a_u = -K_ug a_g
reported_quantity: method + numerical assessment of crossings with arbitrary position/orientation; perturbations; parallel horizontal/vertical coupling
reported_value_and_units: no quantitative values in accessible abstract
prediction_vs_measurement_difference: not applicable (numerical method paper); abstract claims accuracy 'in regimes of low radiative losses'
what_is_direct_evidence: theory: 3D HCMT combines numerically computed eigenmodes of the constituent channels into fully vectorial field approximations; 1D FE discretisation of amplitudes; linear systems for modal amplitudes; examples include perturbations, horizontal/vertical parallel coupling, and crossings of potentially overlapping channels with arbitrary relative positions and orientations; claimed efficient memory, moderate CPU time, accuracy limited to low-radiation-loss regimes

notes: Full text closed (Optica bot-check; Paderborn repository unreachable from this network; Unpaywall: closed). Formulation reconstructed from the published abstract plus the author's publicly available HCMT presentation (computational-photonics.eu/Papers/Pres/wihelp.pdf) - clearly NOT the JOSA B equations. title: Low-loss, low-crosstalk waveguide crossing for scalable integrated silicon photonics applications
material_system: silicon-on-insulator (SOI), 220 nm Si device layer, 2 um buried oxide
index_contrast: high (Si/SiO2; paper does not tabulate bulk indices)
core_dimensions: 500 nm wide strip input/output waveguides; MMI width W_M=1.9 um, MMI length L_M=3.7 um, taper L_T=2.5 um; footprint 14.3x14.3 um2
grid_or_solver_settings: 3D FDTD; eigenmode solver used for effective indices and beat length L_B; mesh accuracy 2-3 in Lumerical knowledge-base workflow (this paper: '3D FDTD simulations were used to perform the optimization' - detailed mesh not reported)
reported_quantity: insertion loss, crosstalk, backscatter
reported_value_and_units: measured IL 43 +/-4 mdB (0.043 dB) per crossing at 1555 nm and 0.044 +/-0.002 dB at 1560 nm; measured crosstalk -50.3 dB at 1550 nm and <= -45.8 dB over 1525-1570 nm; simulated IL 0.042 dB, simulated crosstalk <= -45.6 dB (1520-1580 nm); backscatter best -55 dB
reported_uncertainty: IL +/-4 mdB (1555 nm), +/-2 mdB slope (1560 nm)
prediction_vs_measurement_difference: IL: 0.042 dB simulated vs 0.043-0.044 dB measured (~1-2 mdB). Crosstalk: worst-case simulated -45.6 dB vs measured -45.8 dB over overlapping band (~0.2 dB). Best-case measured crosstalk shows a wavelength offset attributed to structural dimension changes.
what_is_direct_evidence: definitions and validation chain: FDTD -> port projection/S-parameters -> measured cutback IL and through-vs-cross crosstalk; 160-crossing chains measured in time domain; crosstalk measured as relative signal between through and cross ports above the detector noise floor; backscatter measured in frequency and time domain
what_is_our_inference: that the same FDTD/port-projection workflow (not the SOI numbers) is the correct local-model validation template for our crossing; that the agreement level (~1-2 mdB IL, ~0.2 dB crosstalk) is the best case attainable when fabrication is ideal, and that our weak-guide crossings will be harder to measure below -45 dB
notes: Read publisher PDF via Bristol Research Portal (CC BY). Silicon numbers are NOT transferable to glass (see review section 4).

title: All-optical routing and switching for three-dimensional photonic circuitry
material_system: fused silica, femtosecond-laser direct-written (Ti:Sapphire 800 nm, 170 fs, 300 nJ, 100 kHz, NA 0.35)
core_dimensions: elliptical written guides, mode field at 800 nm (approx. 10 um scale); waveguide separation 32 um
grid_or_solver_settings: paraxial (scalar) Helmholtz with measured modal index profiles obtained by inverting the scalar linear Helmholtz equation; cw simulations; sample length 10 cm
reported_quantity: switching contrast, reflection at Y/T junctions, propagation loss
reported_value_and_units: T-junction: ~10 dB switching contrast (exp), ~15 dB (sim); reflection into input ~6 % gated and ~17 % ungated; Y-junction contrast ~9 dB exp vs ~14 dB sim; propagation loss ~0.4 dB/cm
prediction_vs_measurement_difference: simulation over-predicts switching contrast by ~5 dB, attributed to cw vs pulsed excitation dynamics; qualitative intensity patterns correspond well
what_is_direct_evidence: 3D fs-laser-written glass circuits are modelled with split-step BPM using measured index profiles; 90-deg T-junction in glass reflects 6-17 % of power (measured); 32 um centre-to-centre guides are described as 'weakly coupled'; 0.4 dB/cm propagation loss (0.05 dB/cm after thermal treatment quoted from earlier work)
what_is_our_inference: that 3D BPM/SSFM is an accepted forward-propagation engine for glass 3D routing (supports (d)); that reflection at 90-deg junctions in glass is a real loss channel (order 5-15 %) and should not be dropped from the local model; that 32 um separation is already 'weakly coupled' at dn~1e-3, so our 50 um clearances at dn=0.0065 are still likely negligible
notes: PMC full text read. Beam propagation is paraxial; junction effects are modelled phenomenologically via concatenated index profiles.

title: Waveguide crossing (Lumerical Knowledge Base application example, Ansys Optics)
venue: Ansys Optics / Lumerical Knowledge Base, photonic integrated circuits - passive
core_dimensions: not specified in article text (example geometry: four 13-segment polygon arms)
grid_or_solver_settings: FDTD: mesh accuracy 2 for optimisation, 3 for final S-parameter sweep; all boundaries PML for sweep; symmetry BC allowed only for optimisation (symmetry disables ports during S-matrix sweep); port span must cover all modes of interest; broadband single run per port/mode
reported_quantity: definitions and workflow: power transmission to through/cross ports, insertion loss, reflection, S-parameters, energy/consistency checks
reported_value_and_units: no numeric device values in the article (illustrative plots only)
what_is_direct_evidence: how a local crossing device is characterised: ports = mode source + field monitor + mode-expansion monitor; 4-port S-matrix needs one simulation per excited port/mode (or symmetry mapping); figure of merit FOM = T(port3) - T(port2) - T(port4) - R(port1); insertion loss per output port; S-parameters are complex amplitude ratios per mode; INTERCONNECT ONA excites one polarisation at a time; group delay can be added for phase-sensitive circuits; multi-mode S-matrix supported by selecting several modes per port
what_is_our_inference: that our full-board assembly should be built as an S-matrix network (local device S-matrices composed by an N-port circuit solver), and that phase/group-delay bookkeeping matters if coherent crosstalk is to be predicted; that for our few-mode guides the port set must include all guided modes, which multiplies S-matrix size and simulation count
notes: Official vendor documentation, read in full. Numbers in the example are illustrative and not used as benchmarks.

title: Multi-planar amorphous silicon photonics with compact interplanar couplers, cross talk mitigation, and low crossing loss
material_system: amorphous silicon (a-Si) three waveguiding planes, deposited on SiO2; n=3.12 +/-0.1
core_dimensions: 200 nm thick a-Si planes; routed widths 470 nm / 550 nm; interplane pitch 900 nm design (~700 nm fabricated); intraplane pitch 2 um
grid_or_solver_settings: 3D FDTD (details in cited methods; parametric FDTD sweeps around fabricated dimensions)
reported_quantity: out-of-plane crossing loss, interplane coupler loss, inter-plane and intra-plane crosstalk
reported_value_and_units: out-of-plane crossing loss: P1/P3 < 3e-4 dB, P1/P2 3.1e-3 +/-7e-4 dB; interplane coupler 0.05 +/-0.02 dB measured (0.032 dB simulated); crosstalk: -4.8 +/-0.7 dB at 16 um co-propagation for identical-width direct overlap, -12.5 +/-0.7 dB with 80 nm width difference (58 um), -35 +/-0.7 dB for P1/P3 overlapped; intraplane 2 um pitch -> < -19 dB over 2 mm co-propagation
reported_uncertainty: crossing loss +/-7e-4 dB; coupler +/-0.02 dB; crosstalk +/-0.7 dB
prediction_vs_measurement_difference: crossing and coupler losses agree with FDTD at the 1e-3 dB level; the P1/P3 overlapped crosstalk is 16 dB better than FDTD prediction (attributed to fabrication/pitch differences)
what_is_direct_evidence: a quantitative 3D multi-plane study: with sub-micron vertical pitch, direct overlap of modes between planes gives strong crosstalk (-4.8 dB) which is reduced by detuning widths; out-of-plane crossings can be essentially lossless (<3e-4 dB) and crosstalk between co-propagating guides in different planes is governed by mode overlap and phase-velocity mismatch
what_is_our_inference: scaling argument for our 20 planes: overlap between modes 50 um apart is astronomically smaller than the 0.7-0.9 um pitch case, so vertical-offset-driven crosstalk is negligible; the useful transfer is the *method* (crosstalk vs co-propagation length vs width detuning) and the demonstration that crosstalk can be modelled by FDTD and verified experimentally
notes: Read arXiv version 1708.09438 (identical numbers to the published abstract); published version APL Photonics 2, 116101 (2017). Material is high-contrast a-Si - values NOT transferable.

reported_uncertainty: crosstalk quoted as an upper bound only
prediction_vs_measurement_difference: measured -0.16 dB consistent with simulated >95 % transmission; no discrepancy given

what_is_our_inference: that for dn=0.0065 guides the 90-deg crossing itself is a weak perturbation (loss/crosstalk small), so the risk in our board is concentrated at small crossing angles; the -0.16 dB / -40 dB SOI numbers themselves do not transfer
notes: Full PDF read (UGent biblio repository). Note inconsistency in the paper: abstract writes '97.5 % transmission (-1.7 dB)' while the body gives -0.16 dB = 97.5 %; the -1.7 dB figure is an internal typo.

title: Optical loss and crosstalk in multimode photolithographically fabricated polyacrylate polymer waveguide crossings
venue: Proc. SPIE 8988:898807 (Integrated Optics: Devices, Materials, and Technologies XVIII)
material_system: polyacrylate polymer multimode waveguides on FR4 PCB
grid_or_solver_settings: crossing angles 10-90 deg (simulation 10-90 deg in 10 deg steps; experiment 10,15,20,25,30-90 deg); six crossings per test waveguide; source NA 0.22
reported_quantity: loss per crossing vs crossing angle; crosstalk
reported_value_and_units: measured loss per crossing: ~0.14 dB at 10 deg, ~0.079 dB at 20 deg, ~0.043 dB at 40 deg, ~0.030 dB at 60 deg, ~0.021 dB at 90 deg (computed from the paper's fitted expression y=1.078*theta^-0.873 dB, theta in degrees, 10-90 deg); ray tracing predicts >1 dB at <20 deg
reported_uncertainty: 50 repeated measurements per angle; fit line shown but no +/- per point in text
prediction_vs_measurement_difference: ray tracing massively overestimates loss at small angles (>1 dB vs ~0.15 dB at 10 deg); paper attributes this to wave-optical effects ignored by ray tracing
what_is_direct_evidence: for a weakly guiding (~2 %) multimode waveguide, measured crossing loss increases monotonically as the crossing angle decreases (0.02 dB at 90 deg -> 0.15 dB at 10 deg); crosstalk into the crossing arm exists and is angle dependent; ray tracing is unreliable for small angles
what_is_our_inference: that the angle trend (worse at small angle) holds qualitatively for our few-mode 9 um guide; that the absolute magnitudes are not transferable (50 um multimode, dn 0.0296, lambda 853 nm); that our 5-20 deg crossings are the ones needing wave-optics (BPM/FDTD/EME), not ray tracing
notes: Full text read (UCL Discovery). Only weak-contrast angle-resolved measured dataset found; multimode and large core caveat is important.
